title: What Is AI? Rules and Learning
status: Draft practice quiz; teacher review required
instructions: Ten questions. Select all correct options in multiple-choice items. One point for an exact match.

questions.prompt: What makes a fixed thermostat different from a learning system?
options: It explicitly follows a temperature condition
It needs labelled pictures to run
It predicts weather from big datasets
It always uses a neural network
questions.explanation: A conventional thermostat checks a rule written by a person.

questions.prompt: A program explores possible paths in a maze until it finds an exit. Which approach is most directly illustrated?
questions.explanation: A maze solver explores possible states and paths according to rules; it need not be trained.

questions.prompt: A table contains temperature, time of day and the user's desired heating state. What is the target label?
questions.explanation: In supervised learning, the known desired output is the label.

questions.prompt: Six unlabelled objects are divided into two groups by similarity. Which type of learning is this?
questions.explanation: Clustering seeks structure without supplied class labels.

questions.prompt: An agent learns which move to take by receiving rewards after actions. Which training setup does this describe?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning uses reward feedback to improve actions/policies.

questions.prompt: A classifier trained on pictures of notebooks and pencil cases is shown a new notebook. What is happening?
questions.explanation: Using a trained model on a new input is inference.

questions.prompt: Which example is primarily a classical algorithm rather than a learned prediction?
options: A phone learns your favourite next word
A program turns on a lamp when brightness < 200
An image network learns cats from photos
A classifier infers class from learned prototypes
questions.explanation: Checking a fixed threshold is classical control logic.

questions.prompt: What is tokenisation in natural-language processing?
options: Splitting text into tokens such as words or word pieces
Guaranteeing that a sentence is true
questions.explanation: A tokenizer maps text to a sequence of tokens; it does not by itself understand the sentence.

questions.prompt: Select ALL statements that are correct about machine learning.
options: Some models learn from labelled examples
K-Means can discover groups without labels
Every ML algorithm must use a neural network
Perfect training accuracy guarantees correct answers on all new data
questions.explanation: Supervised models may use labelled data, and clustering can use unlabelled data. Neither a neural network nor universal accuracy is guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Select ALL sensible steps when evaluating a trained classroom image classifier.
options: Test ordinary objects not shown during training
Record some failed predictions and possible causes
Only test pictures already used for training
questions.explanation: New test examples and documented errors help evaluate generalisation. Respect privacy and consent.
